text: So, if you are on campus and you walk, as you walk, you may move from one access point to another. You don't realize that, but it happens. And your Wi-Fi card, whenever it connects to a new access point on campus, you will tell during this step: "Look, I was previously connected to this other access point of Tongji University." Okay, and the the access point, the new access point you get connected to, at that point will inform through the distribution system, the previous access point that your user is now connected to that access point. So the previous one understands that you left. This is of course, if you are part of an extended service set. So, as you move, you need to repeat these three steps every time your Wi-Fi card connects to a different access point. And if you are on campus, one of the information that your Wi-Fi card will transmit to the new access point during this step is indeed, "I was connected to this other one." And the new access point will inform the previous access point that you are not there anymore. So this helps to support mobility, user mobility within the same extended service set. Okay, now this exchange of information about themselves, right, to help station access point to get to know each other takes.
